answer: Resist sybils with external-chain anchored identity checkpoints: each new identity must embed its registration in a checkpoint anchored to a busy public chain, like planting one tree in a shared orchard where every sapling pays the same soil fee. A registration counts only after the anchor confirms, so no agent can wander ahead of the queue by minting names in bulk. Reaching the summit of standing needs one anchored checkpoint per identity, each costing real external-chain fees and block space, while an honest agent anchors once and keeps its standing.
